S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar II Disorder is characterized by a recurrent course of major depressive episodes alternating with hypomanic episodes, without any history of full manic episodes. Hypomanic periods involve a noticeable change in mood and energy that is observable by others but typically less severe than mania and not markedly impairing by themselves, though they often precede or follow disabling depressive episodes. The condition often begins in late adolescence or early adulthood and can be precipitated or unmasked by psychosocial stressors, sleep disruption, or substance use. It is distinguished from unipolar depression by the presence of hypomania and from Bipolar I Disorder by the absence of past mania and generally less severe mood elevation, though overall morbidity from recurrent depression can be substantial.

patient.personality: Dwayne is a quiet, precision-focused engineer who enjoys solitary, methodical hobbies and tends to over-plan and worry, favoring predictability and detailed organization in nearly every aspect of life.
patient.stressor: In his late fifties, Dwayne began experiencing age-related health concerns—mild hypertension, joint aches that limited his woodworking and car restoration, and the first serious discussion with his doctor about eventually cutting back work hours. These changes unsettled his long-standing sense of control and predictability; he responded by tightening his routines, tracking every metric of his health, and meticulously reworking retirement budgets and plans. Over time, his family noticed that his mood and energy seemed to shift in phases, with stretches where he became unusually driven and short-tempered about getting projects and health regimens "just right," followed by quieter, withdrawn periods where his usual enjoyment of hobbies and mentoring at the coding meetup faded. After a minor health scare that turned out to be benign but left him feeling uncharacteristically volatile and argumentative at home and at work, his wife suggested that what he was going through didn’t look like his usual worry, leading him to consult a psychiatrist at his primary care provider’s recommendation.
patient.chief_complaint: “My wife says I’ve been more on edge and keyed up than usual, getting irritated over every little thing, and I don’t recognize myself in how I react.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: For the past few weeks I’ve felt like someone turned the dimmer switch down on my mood—most days I just feel flat and discouraged, like I’m watching my own life from the outside and not really caring much about any of it, including the stuff I used to enjoy like tinkering with my car or helping the younger guys at the meetup.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Normally I’m pretty regular with my meals, but lately I’ll look up from my computer at 3 or 4 in the afternoon and realize I’ve basically skipped lunch because nothing sounds appealing and I just don’t feel hungry, and my pants are a bit looser than they were a month ago.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: My sleep has been all over the place, with nights where I lie there for an hour or two replaying health numbers in my head and then wake up at 4 or 5 a.m. staring at the ceiling, feeling like I never really got properly rested even if the clock says I was in bed long enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: My wife keeps pointing out that I’m moving slower, like I’ll stand in the kitchen holding the coffee mug and just stare at the counter before I bother to pour, and even walking up the stairs feels like I’m wading through mud instead of just being a little stiff from my joints.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: At work, something that used to take me an hour—like reviewing a block of code for bugs—now takes most of the morning because my mind keeps fogging up, I reread the same lines over and over, and even deciding how to respond to a simple email feels like more than I can sort out.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: When I’m in one of my ‘up’ phases, especially just before this low stretch started, I feel wired and on edge at the same time—snapping at my wife for tiny things like moving my pill organizer, then fifteen minutes later acting like everything’s great and I’m full of ideas for new projects around the house.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: Right before I dipped into this current funk, I went through a spell where I couldn’t sit still—I was reorganizing all my health spreadsheets, starting three different fixes on the car at once, and pacing around the house because I felt like I had to be doing something every minute.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: In those more revved‑up periods, I catch myself thinking, ‘If I just really focus, I can outsmart this aging thing and get my numbers perfect,’ and I start believing I understand my health better than my doctor does because I’ve been tracking everything so closely.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: During the last ‘keyed up’ stretch, I was only sleeping four or five hours a night, sometimes less, but instead of feeling tired the next day I’d get up before dawn, make coffee, and dive straight into tweaking my retirement spreadsheets or cleaning the garage like I didn’t need sleep at all.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: On those higher-energy days my wife jokes that I’ve turned into a podcast on double speed, because once I start explaining my new workout plan or some idea for reorganizing our budget I just keep talking over her, jumping from one thought to the next without really pausing for breath.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: There are times when I get it in my head that I’m going to ‘optimize everything’ and I’ll suddenly take on extra projects at work, sign up for more mentoring sessions, and map out elaborate exercise and diet schedules all at once, only to realize later that I’ve overcommitted myself again.
